key_insight: A physics-guided deep-learning framework recovers 3D bubble position and physical-equivalent diameter from single-camera shadowgraphs without stereoscopic hardware.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce optical-access, calibration, and hardware demands when measuring bubble distributions that govern transport in multiphase flows.
method: Render DNS-resolved bubbles at multiple focal planes using validated Monte Carlo ray tracing.
Preprocess bubble crops and train a focus-conditioned multitask network to predict signed depth and diameter.
Evaluate held-out predictions, closed-loop DNS reconstruction, and experimental bubble-size distributions.
evidence_signal: Using 900 frames and 87,728 labeled instances split by DNS timestamp, the model achieved approximately 97.6% normalized depth accuracy; experimental size-distribution overlap ranged from 68% to 92%.
watch_item: Reconstruction errors increase with distance from the focal plane, imposing a recoverability limit that must be characterized for deployment.
paper_title: Monocular 3D bubble reconstruction: DNS-informed ray tracing and deep learning
